summary.plannedApproach: Equivalence-class-reduced categorical + numeric matrix, not literal full Cartesian enumeration. See report Section 3 for the explicit reasoning and the technical constraints that drove this scoping decision.
summary.integrityCorrectionNote: An initial consolidation pass produced 110 rows. A pre-publication integrity check (case-ID uniqueness scan) found that case RF-NAR-1000 had been accidentally recorded in both refund_core.json and refund_extra.json as byte-identical duplicate rows (same inputs, same outputs). The duplicate was removed and all downstream files (ledger CSV, evidence JSON, classification counts, this audit) were regenerated against the corrected 109-row dataset before this report was finalized. This is disclosed rather than silently corrected because the directive requires an explicit output-integrity reconciliation step.
summary.caveat: UNTESTED DECLARED CATEGORICAL OPTIONS = 0 refers only to each control's discrete option values (e.g. every disposition, every architecture, every scenario-specific enum value) each being set and run at least once. It does NOT mean every combination (full Cartesian product) of those options was executed -- that was deliberately not attempted; see gaps below.

structurallyNotInstantiableOrExplicitlyO.item: Full Cartesian product of all categorical dimensions per scenario (would require several thousand runs per the prompt's own worked examples)
structurallyNotInstantiableOrExplicitlyO.reason: NOT a structural impossibility of the application -- a resource/tooling constraint of this evaluation. The automation channel available in this session truncates script-return payloads to roughly 1500-2000 characters per call, forcing expensive chunked retrieval for any bulk dataset; a fraction of automated run attempts silently continued executing in the background after the calling tool call reported failure, which on two occasions produced overlapping/racing writes that had to be detected, discarded, and manually re-run in isolation; and the application's own client-side state visibly slowed down (roughly 15x) after ~40-50 uninstrumented runs within one page load, before recovering after a reload. Given these constraints, exhaustively running the multi-thousand-case matrix the prompt describes was not practical within this session; a deliberately curated equivalence-class matrix was substituted and is disclosed here rather than silently passed off as complete.

Not systematically executed as a dedicated ledger. Scenario switches were performed dozens of times informally over the course of the session (every scenario reload/switch) and in every observed instance the scenario description, narrative, and scenario-specific controls updated correctly with no stale text detected -- but this was not captured as a formal per-pair ledger, so it is reported as an informal, non-exhaustive observation rather than a completed matrix.

structurallyNotInstantiableOrExplicitlyO.item: Disposition-switching ordered-transition matrix (up to 30 pairs x 5 scenarios)
structurallyNotInstantiableOrExplicitlyO.reason: Partially covered. One concrete stale-state candidate was found and investigated (ACCESS-V2: a condition possibly leaking from CONDITION into a later RENEW), but the retest with a controlled CONDITION->RENEW pair did not reproduce it, leaving the exact trigger unresolved (see finding F-3 / REVIEW REQUIRED). The full ordered-pair matrix was not executed.

The Import scenario / Export scenario / Export run evidence controls in this application drive native browser file-save and file-open dialogs. This session's browser-automation tools can click the buttons and can supply files to an <input type=file> element via the accessibility tree in some cases, but there is no available mechanism in this environment to intercept a browser 'Save As' download dialog's destination or to independently verify the exported file's byte content without a downloads-folder-capable device bridge, which this session does not have. This is a genuine tooling limitation, not something skipped for convenience: the Export scenario JSON was visually inspected in the scenario-editor textarea (confirmed it contains the full current control state as JSON) but a full export->modify->import->rerun->compare round trip was not completed.

structurallyNotInstantiableOrExplicitlyO.item: Full replay/determinism matrix (60 scenario x disposition x architecture families)
structurallyNotInstantiableOrExplicitlyO.reason: Only 1 of the 60 families was executed via the Replay Last Run control (ACCOUNT-RESTRICTION-V2, RENEW, SAME_LAYER), which returned equivalent:true on all 8 compared dimensions. Not extended to the other 59 families for the same resource reasons above.
